newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh not surprised by death verdict - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: McVeigh not surprised by death verdict - lawyer.

text.p: Timothy McVeigh was not surprised when a jury sentenced him to death Friday for the Oklahoma City bombing, his chief defence lawyer said.
The attorney, Stephen Jones, also said in an interview on "CBS Evening News" that McVeigh did not want to die a martyr's death.
Asked about the death penalty, Jones said: "He was not surprised. He had prepared himself for it."

McVeigh's lawyers had warned him that a quick verdict from the jury was a sign he would receive the death penalty for the bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building on April 19, 1995. The attack killed 168 people.
"We felt the best we could hope for was a divided jury unable to reach a verdict and at that point the judge would sentence him to life without parole," Jones said. "But that was not to be."
Asked if McVeigh wanted to die a martyr, he said: "No, I do not think that would be a correct characterisation of his attitude as I understand it."
Jones said the federal jury could have taken a step toward a "more measured response to acts of domestic disturbance" by sentencing McVeigh to life without parole.
"But I understand it was a difficult decision for them. I'm sure they considered it carefully."
Citing the attorney-client privilege, Jones declined to reveal if McVeigh had ever given any other information about possible co-conspirators in the bombing.

However, he added: "I asked the jurors to spare his life because there is a growing amount of evidence that others were involved in the Oklahoma bombing conspiracy, and they, like the government, would want Mr. McVeigh executed."
"Our experience is that the death penalty does not cause people to talk."
